draft.text: You came in because your right knee feels loose and unstable.
You injured it three days ago while playing soccer.
You heard a pop on the inside of your knee when you tried to plank kick the ball.
Your knee is tender on the inside, especially when pressed.
You have pain when bending or straightening your knee.
You can still walk, but it feels less stable.
You may have an injury to the anterior cruciate ligament, or ACL.
This is a ligament that helps keep your knee stable.
You will have an MRI to check the ACL.
Your doctor will talk to you about the results and next steps after the test.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you hurt your right knee three days ago while playing soccer.
You heard a pop on the inside of your knee when you tried to plank kick the ball.
You have pain that is 6 or 7 out of 10.
It hurts when you press on the inside of your knee.
It is hard to bend or straighten your knee without discomfort.
You may have an injury to your knee, possibly to a ligament called the ACL.
This needs more testing to be sure.
The doctor will order an MRI to check your knee.
You will come back to talk about the results and what happens next.
